subject: Genomex: follow-up on offline/on-prem deployment qualification

Subject: Genomex: follow-up on offline/on-prem deployment qualification

Laura — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what we heard from Genomex:
- Primary requirement: air-gapped on-prem deployment for PHI workflows (no internet egress).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~10 qps with occasional bursts to 25 qps for nightly batch jobs.
- Sequence lengths mostly short (<512 tokens) but some long-form analytics up to 4k tokens.
- Preference: customer-controlled KMS, HSM evaluated later in procurement.

Questions we promised to follow up on (action owners included):
1) Hardware checklist and minimal specs for your steady-state and burst profiles (Mina / Infra).
2) Offline upgrade procedure and how we publish firmware/kernel updates without egress (Soojin / Ops).
3) Network segmentation and switch port requirements for the appliance (Ben / Solutions).
4) Example runbook for day-2 operations and spares list (Mina).

Proposed next steps: 
- I’ll send a concise hardware checklist and an offline upgrade playbook by Wednesday.
- Ben will share port/IP ranges and the minimum firewall rules we need.
- Can we schedule a 30-min call with your infrastructure lead (Tim) and your security contact next week?

Attachments: placeholder for the site-readiness checklist and network diagram — I’ll attach the files in the follow-up email.

Thanks — Mina

--

Thanks Mina — that summary looks right. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- The 25 qps burst is expected during a 2-hour nightly window and must complete within that window.
- The longer 4k token jobs are analytic batch jobs that can be scheduled to run on off-peak windows; latency for them is less critical.
- We do have an internal HSM vendor (SafeVault) and can provide integration details after the procurement phase.

Tim is our infra lead — looping him in. He’s available next week Tue/Thu mornings PT for a 30-min sync.

Laura

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Genomex: hardware checklist + offline upgrade approach (attached)

Tim / Laura — attaching the concise checklist and a proposed offline upgrade approach. Highlights below so it’s easy to scan: 

Hardware checklist (minimal starting config):
- 4 x GPU nodes (A100 80GB or equivalent), each with 1TB NVMe for model shards and paging; 512GB RAM recommended for large batches.
- 2 x control-plane VMs (x86, 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM) for orchestration; Air-gapped network only.
- Dedicated management NICs that can be isolated from data plane for emergency access.
- 2x redundant top-of-rack switches; LACP for critical links.

Storage & spares:
- Spare NVMe (2x per rack) and redundant PSU for each node.
- On-site USB recovery keys for boot firmware.

Offline upgrade flow (high level):
1) Redwood packages signed upgrade bundle (sha256 checksum + PGP signature).
2) We share the bundle via an encrypted transfer to an approved offline media (customer-procured), or via an airgap-approved courier.
3) Customer runs verification steps (checksum + signature) against local HSM/KMS.
4) Staged rollout: canary on a single node -> parallel update -> smoke test -> full rollout.

Notes: we can adapt the packaging to your HSM verification scheme. I attached: site-readiness-checklist.xlsx and redwood-offline-deploy-mop-v1.2.pdf.

Can Ben and Soojin confirm whether the network port list below is sufficient for your firewall team?

Required egress/IPs (for non-airgapped verification only; for air-gapped deployments these are blocked):
- 52.23.10.0/24 (control-plane updates, optional)
- 52.23.11.0/24 (metrics ingestion, optional)

If fully air-gapped, the above can be omitted and updates done via signed bundles only.

Thanks — Mina

Attachment stubs: site-readiness-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 42KB), redwood-offline-deploy-mop-v1.2.pdf (PDF, 280KB)

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Kim <laura.kim@genomex.com>, Tim Lee <timothy.lee@genomex.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Genomex: hardware checklist + offline upgrade approach (attached)

Quick tech clarifications from infra: 
- For the 10 qps steady-state + 25 qps burst target, the recommended starting config is 3 x A100-80GB + 1 x spare node in the same rack to start (we listed 4 earlier to provide headroom). If you have denser GPUs (e.g., H100) we can reduce node count but will need to rebaseline memory and NVMe sizing.
- Networking: we need out-of-band management on a separate VLAN; switch-level ACLs for the management NIC. We only require L2 connectivity between nodes and the orchestration control-plane during normal ops.
- Offline upgrades: we support both media-based bundles and a sealed-signed tarball verified via your HSM. Typical canary window is 30–60 minutes; full rollout can be parallelized across racks depending on redundancy.

Attachment: network-segmentation-diagram.pdf (PDF, 180KB) — shows recommended VLANs, management vs data plane.

Soojin

--

- Tim can take the network diagram to our firewall vendor on Wednesday.

Next steps:

- Ben / Soojin: once Tim confirms port/VLAN questions, set up a 30-min SOC/Infra sync on Thu 24 Mar.

I’ll update the procurement timeline after the PO is initiated. Appreciate the responsiveness — Laura
